cases.expected: non‑null JsonSchema instance whose SchemaLocation string equals "http://example.com/schema" and whose root node matches the supplied JsonNode
cases.description: Happy‑path test: a well‑formed URI and a simple JSON schema node are supplied. The method should create a JsonSchema wrapper without throwing and the internal location should reflect the given URI.

cases.expected: non‑null JsonSchema instance whose SchemaLocation string equals "file:/tmp/my-schema.json" and contains the supplied JSON node
cases.description: Validate that file‑scheme URIs are handled identically to HTTP URIs – the factory must not treat the scheme specially.

cases.expected: non‑null JsonSchema instance whose SchemaLocation string equals "" (empty) and contains the supplied JSON node
cases.description: Edge case where the URI string is empty. The factory should still create a SchemaLocation and not fail.
When the URI argument is null the method should throw NPE because `schemaUri.toString()` is invoked.
When the JsonNode argument is null the method should throw NPE because the node is passed to `newJsonSchema` which expects a non‑null schema node.

cases.expected: non‑null JsonSchema instance whose SchemaLocation string equals "http://example.com/schema.json#/definitions/foo" and whose root node matches the supplied JsonNode
cases.description: Verify that a URI containing an encoded fragment is preserved verbatim in the resulting SchemaLocation.

cases.expected: non‑null JsonSchema instance whose SchemaLocation string equals "schemas/myschema.json" and whose root node matches the supplied JsonNode
cases.description: Test handling of a relative URI (no scheme). The factory should accept it and store the exact string.

cases.expected: non‑null JsonSchema instance whose SchemaLocation string equals "http://example.com/schema.json?v=2&debug=true" and whose root node matches the supplied JsonNode
cases.description: Ensure that query parameters are retained in the SchemaLocation.

cases.expected: non‑null JsonSchema instance whose SchemaLocation string equals "ftp://example.com/remote-schema.json" and whose root node matches the supplied JsonNode
cases.description: Confirm that the factory does not enforce a particular scheme; an FTP URI should be accepted like any other.

cases.expected: non‑null JsonSchema instance whose SchemaLocation string equals "http://example.com/empty-object" and whose root node is an empty ObjectNode
cases.description: Pass an empty JSON object as the schema node; the factory should still create a JsonSchema wrapper.

cases.expected: non‑null JsonSchema instance whose SchemaLocation string equals "http://example.com/array-schema" and whose root node contains an array definition with string items
cases.description: Validate that a typical array schema is accepted without error.

cases.expected: non‑null JsonSchema instance whose SchemaLocation string equals "http://example.com/complex-schema" and whose root node contains the $ref field unchanged
cases.description: Supply a schema containing a $ref to ensure the node is stored verbatim; the factory should not resolve references at construction time.

cases.expected: non‑null JsonSchema instance whose SchemaLocation string equals "http://example.com/primitive-node" and whose root node is a TextNode with value \"just a string\"
cases.description: Pass a JSON primitive (a plain string) as the schema node. The factory should still wrap it without throwing.

cases.expected: non‑null JsonSchema instance and the original JsonNode remains unchanged after the call
cases.description: Ensure that `getSchema` does not mutate the supplied JsonNode. The test captures the node before the call, invokes the method, then verifies the node's content is identical.
